featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited Burma Burma after dinner specifically to try their desserts, having heard a lot about them.

The dessert menu offers some unique creations, and the presentation of each dish is excellent. A lot of thought clearly goes into the plating, making the desserts as visually appealing as they are enjoyable to eat.

Having said that, the Burma Bombe is definitely one for chocolate lovers, as it comes loaded with chocolate.

Overall, if you're a dessert lover, Burma Burma is definitely worth a visit. The combination of innovative flavours and beautiful presentation makes for a memorable dessert experience.

featured_reviews.name: Mudit Bansal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Burma Burma’s Powai outpost brings the highly celebrated flavors of Myanmar directly to Mumbai's bustling suburbs, maintaining the brand's reputation for exceptional 100% vegetarian fare. The restaurant beautifully captures the essence of Burmese culture through a vibrant, lively atmosphere that includes lovely outdoor seating, making it an ideal spot for both casual lunches and special dinners.

An Authentic Culinary Experience
The menu at the Powai branch is a brilliant showcase of Burma Burma's award-winning flavors, turning plant-based dining into a true adventure. Their signature Samosa Soup, a tangy and spicy broth featuring a crisp miniature samosa, is an outstanding way to start the meal and continues to be a crowd favorite. Another unmissable starter is the Steamed Buns filled with brown onion and roasted chili, offering a fluffy texture that is delightfully light on the stomach yet packed with incredible flavor. For the main course, the quintessential Oh No Khowsuey—noodles served in a comforting, rich coconut milk gravy with an array of garnishes—remains the star of the show.

Outstanding Vibe and Service
One of the standout features of the Powai location is the fantastic balance between its modern, vibrant ambiance and authentic culinary roots. To complement the meal, their selection of refreshing beverages, particularly the Burmese Blossom cooler and their unique bubble teas, are highly recommended. Due to the restaurant's immense popularity and exceptional quality, waiting times can stretch up to 40 minutes on weekends since they do not take reservations during peak hours. However, the flawless execution of dishes, the friendly service, and the memorable ambiance make the wait entirely worth it.

featured_reviews.name: Youthika Chauhan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely good food, service and ambience. I've spent a lot of time across Myanmar, and this is the best Burmese food I've eaten outside the eateries in Yangon and Shan State. Perfect place if you are soup lover. Desserts are nice! They customize the dishes if you want like making them less spicy, without mushroom, tofu etc.
They include 10%service fee which is fine given the quality of service. They don't take reservation on weekend.

featured_reviews.review_text:

The dish we liked most is their lotus stem chips and samosa soup it is a must try. The Bao were okk okk bubble tea and the drinks are average.

Mohinga rice bowl is a 20/10 from their festive menu.

featured_reviews.name: Sameen Borker
featured_reviews.review_text: I enjoy eating good food; cuisine and preferences no bar. Given that this is a veg only restaurant, my expectations were medium but they were exceeded. Every dish was flavourful, inventive, and a new experience. You cannot miss the lotus stem chips; they should pack that stuff and sell it on stands. I did not have the khao suey (which is why others usually go there) but I had the sticky rice wrapped in banana leaf (3/5) and the Highway meal (4.5/5) and the pistachio dessert is a 10/5 because its so good we ordered a second one, too. They also had a light dip which looked like yogurt but ended up tasting like coconut; what a packed surprise. Overall, a great experience.

featured_reviews.name: Vijith Shetty
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ambience:

The first thing that strikes you when you enter Burma Burma Powai is its ambience. The restaurant has clearly invested in creating an immersive, warm, and artistic vibe.

The murals on the walls (as seen in the photos) reflect Burmese cultural and architectural elements.

The outdoor seating area looks beautiful with plenty of greenery. The indoor area is lively with comfortable seating.

It’s one of those places where you feel you’re getting a small taste of another culture through the setting. Honestly, the photos don’t capture the full beauty.

Food & Menu:

The menu is the star attraction here — entirely vegetarian and dedicated to authentic Burmese cuisine, something very few restaurants in India offer.

The condiments platter (as seen in the photo) with various dips and chutneys is a nice touch — flavors range from mildly sweet to fiery hot.

If you’re a vegetarian looking to explore new flavors, this is a refreshing change from the usual Asian offerings, but hardcore foodies might expect bolder taste surprises.

Service

The staff is polite and welcoming — they greet you warmly when you arrive.

However, they felt under-trained when it came to explaining dishes. When asked about what to expect from a certain dish, they seemed unsure or lacked confidence.

The service speed could be better — dishes took a little longer to arrive than expected, especially since it wasn’t overly crowded.

Pricing

Prices lean towards the premium side. Some dishes feel slightly expensive considering portion size and overall experience.

It’s fine for a special night out, but if you’re looking for value-for-money comfort food, it may feel a bit heavy on the pocket.

Overall Verdict

Burma Burma Powai is an excellent pick for ambience lovers and vegetarians seeking something different. The interiors are gorgeous and Insta-worthy, the menu is exciting (especially if you’ve never tried Burmese cuisine), and the vibe is great for both small groups and casual dates.

Ambience: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)

Food: ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆ (4/5 — tasty but not unforgettable)

Service: ⭐⭐⭐☆ (3/5 — polite but needs better training)

Value for Money: ⭐⭐⭐☆ (3/5 — slightly pricey)

Overall Rating: 4/5
A good place to experience Burmese vegetarian food in a beautiful setting, though they could polish their service and bring a little more magic to the food to match the prices.

This was one of the worst food experiences I’ve ever had. We were sold stale ladoos at Trupti and Food, and unfortunately my child ate them before we realised they were old. The taste and smell clearly indicated the sweets were not fresh, yet they were still being sold to customers.

What’s even more alarming is that this doesn’t seem like an isolated issue. Most of the food here appears stale, with shelf life seemingly artificially extended just to push sales, without any concern for customer health or safety—especially that of children.

To make matters worse, the manager at the counter was extremely rude and dismissive when this was pointed out. Instead of taking responsibility or apologising, there was arrogance and complete lack of professionalism.

Selling stale food is unacceptable. Selling it to families with kids is downright dangerous. This place needs serious inspection and accountability.

Absolutely do not recommend. Avoid at all costs.

At these prices, one expects quality and trust. Instead, this incident has completely eroded my confidence in this brand. I urge everyone to be extremely cautious when buying from this place, and I request the authorities to look into their food preparation practices.

Trupti, this is not just about a bad experience – it’s about customer safety. Please take responsibility and fix this.

Visited Prasad Food Divine, Powai, Mumbai, for dinner with my family after reading several positive reviews and noticing its fine-dining positioning. Unfortunately, our experience did not live up to the expectations.

The food was just average—neither bad nor exceptional. While the menu offers a good variety of options, the taste did not justify the premium pricing. Service was another area of concern; it was noticeably slow throughout our visit.

One surprising disappointment was that cold mineral water bottles were not available when requested, which is quite unexpected for a restaurant that presents itself as a fine-dining establishment.

Another major concern was the ambiance. During our dinner, there were two birthday celebrations with loud recorded songs and significant noise levels. While celebrations are understandable, a fine-dining restaurant is generally expected to provide a calm, comfortable, and relatively private dining atmosphere. The excessive noise disturbed the overall experience and made it difficult to enjoy a relaxed family dinner.

Overall, the ambiance is decent, but considering the food quality, service, noise levels, and pricing, we did not find good value for money. Based on our experience, the restaurant did not meet the expectations associated with a fine-dining destination. Hoping the management addresses these concerns and improves the overall guest experience.

featured_reviews.review_text:
The dining experience was defined by a profound lack of balance and technical incompetence in basic preparation. The focus on presentation failed to compensate for the fundamental disregard for flavor profiles and texture.
​Spaghetti Pangrattato and Burrata: A failure in seasoning. The excessive salinity rendered the dish inedible, overpowering the intended pesto profile and demonstrating a lack of quality control in the kitchen.
​Bibimbap: A technical failure regarding the core ingredient. The integrity of the rice—the foundational element of the dish—was compromised to the point of being a mashed, unappealing starch. This lack of structural integrity destroyed the dish's identity.
​Spinach Ravioli: While un-tasted, the pervasive lack of execution across the previous courses created a clear expectation of failure, further cementing the lack of confidence in the kitchen's capabilities.
​Core Recommendation:
Stop prioritizing surface-level aesthetics. A restaurant’s reputation must be built on the palate, not the plate's appearance. You are currently sacrificing the integrity of your ingredients for the sake of trends. Return to the basics: master the seasoning of your sauces and the texture of your grains. Until the technical execution matches the visual branding, this establishment will remain an exercise in disappointment.

The Wadapav Cafe- Elite, a new opened outlet at Powai serving some of the best Mumbai street foods. Tried multiple options that they had to offer on one fine rainy evenings.

Classic Wadapav, was a go to option. the wada was good in taste and had a fine crisp to it. Alu Wadi, one of Maharashtra's famous snacks made from colocasia leaves and chickpea flour, liked it very much. Kothimbir Wadi, another famous bites, made from crushed coriander, yogurt and gram flour, this is a great munchy, loved it!. Later, tried Puran Poli, my favorite of them all. they are these sweet heavenly rotis with jaggery fillings. This one was made with so full of love and ghee. Excellent! Not to forget the Mango Shake that was served, apt in thickness and left an awesome after-taste.

Having so many outlets in Powai can be confusing, but this place surely deserves a try. Get on it!

​Food & Drinks
​The menu is impressively diverse. We had a mix of Asian and Continental dishes—the sushi and dim sum were incredibly fresh, and the small plates are perfect for sharing in a group setting. The cocktail program is also top-notch; the mixologists really know their craft.
​Service
​The staff handled our group with total professionalism. Even with a packed house, the service was prompt, and they went out of their way to ensure the celebration went smoothly.
​Bottom Line: Whether it’s a corporate mixer, a birthday, or just a big get-together with friends, Eve offers the right balance of class and fun. Easily one of the best spots in the neighborhood right now!

featured_reviews.name: Sapaatu Payanam
featured_reviews.review_text:
Just visited Mejwani Maharashtrichi in Powai, Mumbai for lunch and it turned out to be a proper Maharashtrian feast! If you love authentic regional food, this place is definitely worth trying.

Started the meal with Kothimbir Vadi – perfectly crisp on the outside and soft inside, packed with coriander flavor. A classic Maharashtrian snack done right.

Next came the Chicken Pahadi and Kabab. The Chicken Pahadi had a nice smoky flavor with mild spices, while the Kabab was juicy, tender, and grilled beautifully. Great starters to kick off the meal.

For the main course, I tried Valacha Birda and Maswadi. Valacha Birda, a traditional Maharashtrian curry made with field beans, had a rich, earthy taste. Maswadi was unique and flavorful, with its spiced gram flour dumplings soaking up the curry perfectly.

Paired everything with Jawari Bhakri, which tasted fresh and authentic – a perfect match for the curries. Also had Green Salad and Steam Rice on the side to balance the meal.

Ended the lunch on a sweet note with Kharvas, a traditional Maharashtrian dessert made from colostrum milk. It was soft, mildly sweet, and flavored with cardamom – the perfect way to finish the meal.

Overall, a satisfying experience with authentic flavors that truly represent Maharashtrian cuisine. If you’re in Mumbai and want to try traditional dishes beyond the usual restaurant menus, this place is definitely worth visiting.

The location is unbeatable—right in the heart of the Hiranandani ecosystem. It’s thoughtfully placed amidst a vibrant yet serene environment, with easy access to markets, restaurants, and relaxing evening spots. After long business meetings, taking a stroll through the nearby market was the perfect way to unwind. The area has a unique charm, blending convenience with calmness.

The team at the Parabola restaurant deserves special mention. Ashiyan, Komal, and Karan were incredible hosts, curating an exceptional dining experience that made my stay all the more enjoyable. They took the time to understand my preferences and presented the best options with impeccable hospitality. Their dedication to making guests feel cared for is unmatched.

The hotel itself is a reflection of high standards, from the well-appointed rooms to the seamless service. It’s clear that every detail has been thoughtfully designed to cater to business travelers. The ambiance strikes the right balance between professionalism and comfort, making it an ideal place to relax and focus.

We tried multiple dishes at Bayroute and overall had a very pleasant experience.
The Machboos Al Kuzu was flavourful and aromatic, with beautifully spiced rice and tender lamb — a very satisfying and hearty dish.

The hummus with chicken shawarma add-on and pita bread was absolutely awesome. The hummus was creamy and rich, the shawarma was well-seasoned, and together with warm pita bread it tasted amazing.

The Kuzu (lamb dish) was cooked well and the meat was tender. It was tasty and comforting, though the flavours were on the milder side and felt a little subtle.

The baklava was a complete show, waiter crushed rose on it and  made it feel special, and it tasted amazing. Rich, flaky, and not overly sweet.

Overall, the place is slightly heavy on the pocket, but the ambience is very good, the location is convenient, and the staff is friendly and helpful, which adds a lot to the experience.
I really liked the place and would visit again.

Bayroute, Powai, is a Middle Eastern dream come true! 🌅 The ambience is a warm mix of indoor & outdoor seating, with hot air balloons 🛫️ setting the perfect Middle Eastern vibe — super cozy and Instagram-worthy! 👌 Staff are friendly & attentive, and the washrooms are spotless.

Food Highlights:
- Fateh Dajaj: Succulent shredded chicken in a creamy garlic sauce with crispy bread — addictive & finger-licking good!
- Kebab Halabi: Soft, fresh bread paired with juicy kebabs — a match made in heaven.
- Lavash Crush Chicken Halabi: A biryani-like delight, mild on spice, with lavash crust (crunchy like papad) adding that wow factor.
- Dijaj Tria: A trio of chicken preparations — perfect for those wanting a taste of variety.

Desserts & Drinks:

- Greek Goddess (drink): Refreshing light berry drink — perfect for a chill vibe.

- Salted Caramel Baklava Sheikh*: My fav! Rich, nutty, and that salted caramel twist on classic baklava — divine. Remeber to share it cz it is heavy!

- Kunafa (live experience): Layers of crunchy pastry, dry fruits, and ice cream — utterly mesmerizing & drool-worthy.

Verdict: Bayroute’s food, ambience, and live kunafa prep make it a must-visit for Middle Eastern food lovers! Hot air balloons, good staff, and clean washrooms — they’ve ticked all the boxes. ⭐️

For non car goers they can jst get off at Vikhroli station, and get an auto for supreme business park for approx 100rs.

Definitely recommended.

featured_reviews.name: Ajesh Vengara
featured_reviews.review_text: Very good Japanese and Korean food. Service is good. Manager is very helpful. Location is little difficult to find, you need to speak with security guards to reach the exact location. Restaurant has rest room. There is valet parking.

featured_reviews.name: ASWANTH T S
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Origami this evening and had an absolutely fantastic experience! I tried their Kimchi Jjigae with Pork (Authentic Korean Kimchi Stew) — rich, spicy, and bursting with the deep, tangy flavor of perfectly fermented kimchi. The pork was tender and cooked to perfection, making each bite incredibly satisfying.

To complete the meal, I had a bottle of original Jinro Soju — smooth, clean, and the perfect pairing with the stew. It truly felt like a taste of Korea right here in the city.

If you're looking for authentic Korean food, Origami delivers the real deal. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Kajal
featured_reviews.review_text: The ambience is so peaceful and pretty, and the service is good with polite staff. The food we tried-  Korean ramyun was fine but bland, while the shrim tempura was the standout, flavourful with a perfect crunch, fried chicken was a lil sweeter but still nice. The mocktails and sides Kimchi, Bean sprouts, Natto  were also pretty good too. Overall it's a great spot for exploring japanese and korean cuisine.

featured_reviews.name: Mamta Negi
featured_reviews.review_text: The server was quite good , he was explaining every dish and giving clear details if the dish will be sweet or spicy.  The only issue was food was taking so long. They should work better on service. And give hot food. Even the ramen and  side dish  served were cold which we really not expected. We only like kimbap and rest food was ordinary, we have tasted better food other places. If you are going for korean food and taste is also not great,They have limited options but  mostly japanese food.

featured_reviews.name: Indradeep Roy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Located inside Supreme business park. Do check at the gate how to drive in else the entry is bit confusing. Valet parking available.

The food is quite authentic. They specialises in both Japanese and Korean dishes. The quality of food is outstanding and surely recommend to patrons who loves such cuisines.

The set up of the restaurant is quite humble and decor minimum. Clearly their focus is on food rather than decor.

I really loved their sushi and Ramen noodles.

featured_reviews.name: J S
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is a small restaurant in a commercial building. The ambience is not the best, expect a few funky smells and clustered seating. Udipi style ambience and service staff but smelly.

We tried quite a few things and found their salmon carpaccio to be the best of the lot.

They could not do the pan grilled fish and promised pan fried fish which came out deep fried.

The salmon nigri sushi had a thin sliver of salmon on a whole lot of rice.

The tempura was with a hard coating without any salt.

The worst thing is the fact that they are really expensive for what they offer.

Absolutely Avoid.
